q: An extinct volcano rising out of the Rhine plain, capped with terraced loess, records some of the highest temperatures in German viticulture. What is it called?
exp: Volcanic rock underlies deep wind-blown loess on the Kaiserstuhl, and the combination holds heat remarkably well. Spatburgunder and Grauburgunder are what it is planted to.

q: In the far south of Baden, near Basel, growers work a soft, neutral old variety that Switzerland calls Chasselas. What is its German name?
exp: Gutedel gives a low-acid wine drunk young and almost entirely locally, and the Markgraflerland is effectively its only German home. Klingelberger is the Ortenau's name for Riesling, and Rulander is Pinot Gris in a richer style.

q: A squat, flattened flagon quite unlike any other German bottle marks the wine of one region. Which?
exp: The Bocksbeutel is protected for Franken and for two pockets of Baden, the Taubertal in the north and the Neuweier vineyards near Baden-Baden. It will not lie down in a rack and is instantly recognisable across a room, which is rather the point.

q: Which grape is Franken's signature, bottled dry and showing an earthy, herbal, almost savoury cast?
exp: Silvaner ripens earlier than Riesling, which matters badly in Franken's short continental season, and it takes its character from limestone and gypsum marl. Franken finishes it dry almost without exception.

q: Shell limestone laid down in a shallow tropical sea underlies the best vineyards around Wurzburg. What is that rock called?
exp: Muschelkalk gives the taut, stony Silvaner of the Stein and its neighbours above the town. Keuper, a gypsum-rich marl, takes over further east around Iphofen and gives a broader, softer wine.

q: Twelve of the thirteen Anbaugebiete sit in EU wine zone A and one sits in the warmer zone B. What does that difference change for the grower?
opts: A lower ceiling on enrichment of the must in zone B
A longer minimum ageing period before release in zone B
A higher permitted yield per hectare in zone B
Permission to irrigate an established vineyard in zone B
exp: Zone A allows enrichment of up to 3.0% vol and zone B only 2.0%, so the warmer zone may add less sugar before fermentation. Baden is the region concerned, and its warmth is exactly why the allowance is smaller.

q: A German white arrives with searing acidity, lime and green apple, a whiff of kerosene once it has age, and it mirrors its vineyard more faithfully than almost any grape. Which variety?
exp: Riesling ripens very late, which is why it needs the best slopes Germany has, and it holds acidity even when fully ripe. The petrol note comes from a compound that builds in bottle and is a marker of the grape rather than a fault.

q: Grauburgunder and Rulander appear on German labels for one and the same grape. What separates the two names in practice?
opts: Grauburgunder signals a dry style and Rulander a richer, sweeter one
Rulander is a modern crossing and Grauburgunder is not
Grauburgunder is grown in the north and Rulander in the south
exp: Both are Pinot Gris. The split is convention rather than law, but a bottle marked Rulander is usually the fuller, sweeter interpretation and Grauburgunder the crisp dry one.

q: Which German name should you look for on a label to find Pinot Noir?
exp: Spat means late and the Burgunder suffix marks the Pinot family, so Grauburgunder is Pinot Gris and Weissburgunder Pinot Blanc. Spatburgunder is the most widely planted red variety in Germany.

q: A German crossing bred in Wurttemberg in the 1950s was designed above all to put colour into pale red blends, and became a variety in its own right. Which?
exp: Dornfelder gives a dark, soft, plummy wine with little tannin, made both as an everyday red and, from lower yields, in a more ambitious barrel-aged style. It stands second only to Spatburgunder among Germany's red plantings.

q: A dry German white shows quiet pear and green herbs, moderate acidity and a stony finish, and is the traditional partner for white asparagus. Which variety?
exp: Silvaner's softer acidity and mild aromatics leave the vegetable alone instead of fighting it, and Spargelzeit in May is when Germany drinks most of it. Riesling's acidity and Scheurebe's grapefruit both trample the dish.

q: Which German crossing gives a pungent white smelling of grapefruit and blackcurrant, and is bottled sweet as readily as dry?
exp: Scheurebe was bred in Rheinhessen from Riesling and a partner only identified much later, and its aromatics survive right up into Beerenauslese. Overcropped or underripe it smells frankly of cat, which is why it is planted less than it once was.

q: Two bottles of German Riesling both say Spatlese on the label; one is bone dry and one is sweet. What is that word actually recording?
opts: The sugar in the grapes at harvest
The sugar left in the finished wine
The length of ageing before the wine was released
The calendar date on which the fruit was picked
exp: Pradikat is a must weight, measured before fermentation begins. What becomes of that sugar afterwards is the winemaker's decision, so a Spatlese trocken and a sweet Spatlese start from the same place and end up somewhere different.

q: Put the rungs in order: which sequence runs from the lowest must weight upward?
exp: Each rung demands more sugar in the fruit than the one below it, and the minimum figures differ by region and by grape. Eiswein sits alongside Beerenauslese in must weight, with Trockenbeerenauslese at the top.

q: German must weight is read on a nineteenth-century scale that measures the density of the juice against water. What is that scale called?
exp: One degree Oechsle is the number of grams by which a litre of must outweighs a litre of water. Baume is the French scale, Brix the American and KMW the Austrian, and all four are reading the same thing.

q: Adding sugar to the must before fermentation is allowed for German Qualitatswein but forbidden outright at one level. Which?
exp: The entire point of the ladder is that the sugar came out of the vineyard, so enrichment would make the claim meaningless. Lower down the pyramid, where no ripeness claim is being made, it is permitted.
